subject: Strategic readiness: needle-movers, risks, and specific help requests
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Strategic readiness: needle-movers, risks, and specific help requests

Team —

Quick weekly readout ahead of QBR prep. I focused this note on 3 needle-movers we should prioritize, the top operational risks, and two narrowly scoped asks where I need quick support. Keep replies short — just say "OK" or provide the item below if you own it.

Wins (small, high-impact):
- Hosted API latency P95 improved 14% after the priority kernel swap (infra note attached).
- Team shipped the embeddings cache layer for low-cardinality queries (saves ~18% token cost on pilot).
- New Dedicated onboarding flow reduced setup time from 7d -> 2d in our pilot with Acme.

Top Risks (impact + mitigation):
1) Dedicated pool exhaustion in us-west on peak windows — risk: customer throttles and SLA misses. Mitigation: short-term bursting to shared pools, MA plan to expand capacity in dedicated clusters. Need: ops approval for temporary burst allocation (see attachment: capacity-request-form.docx).
2) One regression in the new quantized kernel impacted longer-context generation for >1% of evaluation prompts. Mitigation: rollback toggle available; we need a decision on whether to rollback or ship filters.
3) Several customer security questionnaire asks pending evidence (SOC scope). Risk: delays in renewals for enterprise prospects.

Asks (concrete, owners, ETA):
- Markus: approve a 72-hour burst to dedicated_us_west (details in capacity-request-form.docx). ETA: EOD Tue.
- Laura: confirm we should rollback the quantized kernel for GA models or apply a patch that ships tonight (I recommend patch + monitoring). ETA: EOD Tue.
- Maya: prioritize SOC evidence doc completion for two renewal accounts (Acme + CloudMarket). Can you confirm resource assignment? ETA: Wed COB.

Attachments: QBR_pulse_deck_v3.pdf (summary deck), infra_incidents_202704.xlsx (incident timeline), capacity-request-form.docx (burst details).

Next steps: I will consolidate replies into a final decision thread on Wed and prepare a 1-slide ask for exec.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:20:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategic readiness: needle-movers, risks, and specific help requests

Thanks for the clear note. Quick replies:
- Approve the burst in principle, but need a headcount / cost estimate for CFO signoff. Hannah, can you/ops add a 1-paragraph cost summary?
- On the quantized kernel: prefer patch + monitoring unless the rollback is trivial (if rollback is <2h ops work we should do it).

I'll be on PTO tomorrow morning; if you need rapid approval I can grant delegated signoff to Vivek for the burst.

-Markus

Subject: Re: Strategic readiness: needle-movers, risks, and specific help requests

Team —

Agree with Hannah's prioritization. A couple of clarifying points and a small escalation:

- SOC evidence: Maya, please include the e-evidence for logging retention and the audit trail extract. Acme specifically called this out in their renewal.
- Dedicated pool burst: I want legal to sign off on any customer-impacting fallback before we push burst to shared pools. Looping in Acme sales for transparency (sales@acme-enterprises.com).

Escalation: the pilot with Acme showed one config edge-case that could repeat if we do a blind burst — we need a short test window with a canary before routing real Acme traffic to shared pools. Ops: please plan a 2hr canary between 1-3AM PT and report metrics.

Laura
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Strategic readiness: needle-movers, risks, and specific help requests

Hannah / team —

Quick operational update:
- Burst request: approved. I authorized a 72-hour burst to dedicated_us_west. Ops has scheduled a canary for Tue 02:00-04:00 PT (two-hour window) and will route no more than 5% of Acme test traffic.
- Cost summary: estimated incremental cost = $12k for 72h (GPU time + ephemeral infra). Tagged a budget line to "QBR-ops-burst" for accounting.
- Kernel regression: infra pushed a patch last night; we ran a limited eval and saw the failure rate drop to 0.1%. I recommend we ship the patch and monitor for 48h.

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QzQBR_pulse_v3 (pulse deck), Jira OPS ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1821

Vivek

Thanks all — consolidated update and next steps below (finalizing slide for Wed QBR):

Decisions:
- Burst approved and scheduled (Vivek); cost estimate noted ($12k). Ops to run 2hr canary and report metrics to the QBR channel.
- Kernel: patch approved and will be monitored for 48h. No rollback.
- SOC evidence: Maya to lead, Laura to review. Deadline: Wed COB.

Deliverables for QBR slide (owners):
- Hannah: 1-slide summary + 1 backup slide with cost details and sequence for the burst. (Done draft, see Drive link).
- Vivek: canary metrics + final cost reconciliation post-burst.
- Maya: SOC evidence checklist + note on renewal impact.

Open asks (short):
- Markus: confirm delegated signoff for anything >$25k overnight if you're not available.
- Legal: (Laura) ask legal to review the burst fallback language — can you confirm by EOD?

Thanks — I'll send the final slide set by Tue morning so we can rehearse.

Hannah

Director, Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference
